content: The CWMA had, on August 25, upheld the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee’s recommendation directing Karnataka to ensure a flow of 9,000 cusecs to Tamil Nadu for 15 days; on release of backlog of water, the top court asks Tamil Nadu to challenge the CWMA decision

title: India’s GDP growth at 7.8% in Q1, slower than last quarter but quicker than last year
content: The stronger performance in Q1 of this year as compared to last year has been driven by the manufacturing sector as well as some broad services categories such as utilities, financial services, real estate, IT, and public administration and defence.

title: India’s GPS problem: Why the armed forces need NavIC to work
content: India's NavIC satellite system, crucial for military and civilian use, currently has only three operational satellites. This shortfall impacts its ability to provide accurate positioning and navigation services. The system's reliability issues stemmed from imported atomic clocks, now being replaced by indigenous ones. Upcoming launches aim to restore the full constellation's functionality. This indigenous capability is vital for India's strategic autonomy and modernization efforts.

title: No roofs, no toilets, no teachers: TOI check finds minuses in Rajasthan govt schools
content: TOI reporters visited govt schools in 6 Rajasthan districts after the CJP row. The findings show how basic govt schooling has collapsed in pockets of the state, from the coaching capital of Kota to desert villages and Jhalawar’s tragedy-hit Piplodi.

title: Major shake-up in Pakistan cricket: Seven players, coaches Sarfaraz, Gul released
content: Following a string of losses, the Pakistan Cricket Board has made significant changes by releasing seven players and parts of the coaching staff. Five new uncapped players have been brought on board, while Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul step aside from their coaching positions. Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke will now oversee the coaching duties as the team readies itself for the third Test match against England at Edgbaston.

title: Oracle layoffs: Company leadership may again send the '6 am' email on September 1
content: Oracle employees expect layoff emails on September 1, the day its fiscal second quarter begins, with managers asked to submit lists of affected employees and some teams facing double-digit cuts. Staff fear a repeat of March 31, when a 6 am email from "Oracle Leadership" told 10,000 workers their role was eliminated. Oracle has already cut 21,000 jobs this fiscal year while spending $55.7 billion on AI data centres.

title: From exam reforms to school reforms: How CJP is changing political discourse
content: Student protests for improved school conditions have shifted from cities to villages across India.  The Cockroach Janata Party's campaign exposed poor government school infrastructure in several states.  State governments responded with new regulations and accelerated development projects.  Political parties are now focusing on youth outreach and educational issues.  This movement highlights youth as potential game-changers in electoral politics.

title: 43km, 0 stops & defunct CCTV: Security gaps exposed in Delhi-NCR bus gang rape case
content: A heartbreaking incident in Greater Noida has emerged, where a 16-year-old girl was reportedly gang-raped by a bus driver and conductor. After picking her up during a rainstorm, the assailants left her stranded near Kashmere Gate post-assault. The police responded promptly, capturing the culprits by tracking the bus, evoking memories of the Nirbhaya case that shocked the nation.

title: OpenClaw that Sam Altman spent billions on gets 'largest update in its history'
content: OpenClaw has unveiled its most comprehensive software upgrade yet with the arrival of version 2.0. This update enhances user accessibility significantly and integrates features for multi-user collaboration. Installation has been streamlined, along with expanded cross-platform automation tools. The redesigned browser interface provides a centralized workspace that improves navigation, while sophisticated routines and enhanced information retrieval tools elevate the overall user experience.

title: US signs 7-year deals to boost THAAD & Patriot missile production
content: The Pentagon has secured seven-year agreements with defense contractors. These deals aim to increase production of critical missile subcomponents. This effort supports the THAAD and PAC-3 MSE interceptor programs. The agreements will strengthen the missile defense industrial base. Higher production volumes and faster deliveries are now expected.

title: Two Canadian builders turn 612,000 bottles into hurricane-resistant home
content: In an innovative project, builders in Nova Scotia have successfully created a house using recycled plastic bottles. These bottles were reshaped into high-performance composite panels, exemplifying the practicality of recycled materials in modern construction. The panels not only endured severe wind conditions but also showcased the durability and efficiency of transforming waste into robust building solutions.

title: On his last day as Apple CEO, Tim Cook sends memo to employees
content: Tim Cook has sent his final memo to Apple employees on his last day as CEO, telling staff he is not leaving Apple but stepping away from a role he loved. John Ternus takes over as Apple CEO on September 1, while Cook becomes executive chairman. Read Tim Cook's full memo, his praise for Ternus, and what the handover means for Apple's hardware-first next chapter.

title: India name 26-member squad for big friendlies against Brazil, Uruguay and Panama
content: India's head coach Khalid Jamil has officially unveiled a 26-member squad as the team gears up for an intense series of international matches. The Blue Tigers will challenge themselves against esteemed squads from Panama, Brazil, and Uruguay. This series serves as a prime opportunity to evaluate the team's strengths against formidable rivals.

title: Badshah, Isha Rikhi announce divorce after five months of marriage
content: Rapper Badshah and actress Isha Rikhi have officially announced their separation after weeks of swirling rumors. They revealed the news via similar statements on their Instagram Stories. This marks the end of Badshah's second marriage; he has a daughter from his first. The couple urged for privacy and requested a halt to any further speculation about their lives.

title: D4vd’s private lawyers withdraw from case: Why did he switch to a public defender?
content: D4vd’s private attorneys have withdrawn from representing him in the murder case involving 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. During an August 31, 2026 hearing, the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office was appointed as his new legal team. Burke has pleaded not guilty, remains jailed without bail and faces multiple charges. After a July preliminary hearing found enough evidence for trial, his next court appearance is expected in October 2026.

title: Aaron Donald returns to Rams: Can he and Myles Garrett form the NFL’s best duo?
content: Aaron Donald’s comeback to the Los Angeles Rams for the 2026 season marks a thrilling return from retirement. Joining forces with the talented edge Myles Garrett, they form an intimidating pass rush that will test the mettle of any quarterback. With aspirations of clinching a Super Bowl title in their home stadium, this partnership heralds a fresh wave of defensive excellence for the Rams, reviving hopes for passionate fans.

title: Messi’s 10 most iconic moments as Argentina legend retires from int'l football
content: Lionel Messi has decided to retire from international football at 39, marking the end of an extraordinary era for Argentina. After an impressive career spanning nearly two decades, Messi guided his national team to triumph in the 2021 Copa America and the 2022 World Cup, as well as reaching the final of the 2026 World Cup. His departure signifies a deeply emotional farewell to a remarkable journey.

title: Rohit Sharma show premiere set: Cricketer makes TV debut with Family Full House
content: Rohit Sharma is set to grace television screens with his debut show, 'Family Full House,' which will air on September 19, 2026. As fans eagerly await the iconic cricketer's signature dialogues, he remains active in ODIs while stepping back from other cricket formats. The channel will also be home to beloved shows like 'Kaun Banega Crorepati' and the 'Indian Game Show.'

title: ‘Where are the jobs?’ Congress challenges PM Modi after 7.8% Q1 GDP growth data
content: India's economy grew by 7.8 percent in the April-June quarter. Congress questioned the growth's impact on jobs and prosperity. Prime Minister Modi described the performance as an exemplary and herculean feat. Opposition leaders cited concerns about investment and consumer confidence. They also highlighted issues like unemployment and falling real wages.

title: Nepal floods: Avalanche raced down Himalayas at 167 kmph, triggering deadly deluge
content: A sudden ice-rock avalanche plummeted down the Himalayas, wreaking havoc in Nepal with catastrophic floods. This swift phenomenon covered extensive ground in mere moments, and scientists ruled out a glacial lake outburst flood as the cause. The disaster wreaked havoc on Nepal's hydropower facilities, prompting a call for further inquiries into the geological processes that led to this calamity.

title: Gold pledged for loan stolen in bank robbery: How borrower won case for full value
content: So, what happens if gold jewellery pledged against a gold loan is stolen from the bank? For a borrower, the loss can raise a bigger question than simply recovering the value of the gold. Should the bank pay only for the metal, or should the compensation also cover making charges and the value of stones?

title: Why is it illegal to take sand from some beaches? Reasons you should know
content: Removing sand from beaches carries hefty penalties due to its dire environmental consequences. Destinations like Sardinia and Hawaii impose stringent laws against the extraction of sand, pebbles, or shells, as these elements play a crucial role in combating coastal erosion and nurturing marine life. In India, rampant illegal sand mining devastates neighborhoods and ecosystems alike, exhausting this precious resource and igniting lasting repercussions.

title: ‘I don’t have anything more to give’: Lionel Messi retires from int'l football
content: Lionel Messi has officially announced his retirement from international football, wrapping up a remarkable chapter in his illustrious career. He described this decision as both difficult and necessary, highlighting the timing as crucial. In his statement, Messi expressed deep appreciation for his fans, noted the significance of nurturing emerging young players, and leaves the sport with fulfillment and dignity.

title: Vance says Trump’s dramatic Kharg Island post was meant as a signal to Iran
content: US Vice President JD Vance stated Donald Trump's social media post conveyed a message to Iran.  American military officials confirmed no strikes occurred on Kharg Island overnight.  An Iranian official dismissed Trump's post as laughable and not credible.  US forces did attack two Iranian launchers on Larak Island recently.  These developments renew security concerns in the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Pakistan crisis deepens after Lord’s rout: Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq set to return home
content: Following a string of embarrassing losses to England, significant changes are on the horizon for Pakistan's Test team. Reports indicate that wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan and opener Imam-ul-Haq will be sent back home. In light of the team's disappointing performance, senior officials from the Pakistan Cricket Board convened for an urgent meeting to address rising concerns over both players and coaching strategies.

title: ‘Uncertainties’ rising: Xi calls for stronger cooperation in meeting with Putin
content: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping met at the SCO summit. They discussed strengthening bilateral ties and international regional issues. Cooperation in artificial intelligence and digital innovation was also a key topic. Russia proposed making the bilateral visa-free regime permanent for Chinese citizens. The leaders also touched upon the Ukraine conflict during their talks.

title: Sobhana Mostary recalls the India win that ‘changed everything’ for Bangladesh
content: Sobhana Mostary believes Bangladesh’s 2018 Asia Cup triumph over India brought a huge change in women’s cricket in her country, with greater facilities and financial support. From moving to Dhaka as a young cricketer to waiting years for regular opportunities, Mostary has steadily grown into a dependable international batter. She also recalls how Harmanpreet Kaur’s batting inspired her and why facing India remains exciting for Bangladesh.

title: US PrSM missiles in Iran strike killed civilians up to 50 metres away: Report
content: On February 28, a series of strikes in Lamerd, Iran, resulted in the tragic loss of at least twenty-one civilians. It is believed that US-manufactured Precision Strike Missiles facilitated the deadly attack, as these weaponry disperse dense tungsten pellets rapidly in various directions. While the US military has confirmed the use of PrSMs in Iranian operations on that date, they have disavowed any specific targeting of Lamerd.

title: Nepal tragedy: Owners missing, dog refuses to leave flood-hit Trishuli home
content: A black-and-white dog remains at the site of four homes destroyed by a flood.  He refuses to leave the muddy patch where his home once stood.  Rescue workers and JCBs clear debris around the steadfast canine.  Volunteers offer food and water, which he accepts quietly when alone.  Displaced residents understand his loyalty to his former territory.

title: NPS charges change Oct 1: Rs 200 fee, 0.20% annual charge; who pays?
content: Under the new fee structure, subscribers registering for NPS through a PoP will be charged a one-time onboarding fee of Rs 200 for each Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN). However, the entire Rs 200 will not be taken from the subscriber’s account at once.

title: Mumbai property registrations hit 14-year August high at 12,401 units
content: In August, Mumbai experienced an impressive eleven percent rise in property registrations year-on-year, marking the highest number for the month in over fourteen years. This surge indicates strong demand in both the primary and secondary housing markets. Ongoing buyer interest and favorable economic factors bolster the market's resilience, urging developers to emphasize project execution as they introduce new launches for sustained success.

title: 'Umpires' calls & different ball': Root explains lean run as he chases Sachin’s record
content: Joe Root remains confident despite a difficult batting summer for England. He believes challenging conditions and the Dukes ball have impacted all batters. Root has scored only twice over fifty this season, averaging 29.44. He is still focused on surpassing Sachin Tendulkar's Test run record. England secured a series win against Pakistan under his captaincy.

title: Tamil Nadu announces major housing reforms, Rs 2,883 crore plan to rebuild flats
content: Tamil Nadu announced initiatives to streamline building approvals and digitize land-use processes. Self-certification will expand for residential and small commercial buildings. Local body approval limits for residential and commercial projects are also increasing. A significant plan will rebuild 12,648 dilapidated flats across twenty project areas. The government will also introduce interest relief schemes for housing loan borrowers.

title: US Open: Mariano Navone wins battle as Novak Djokovic’s body says no
content: Mariano Navone pulled off an incredible upset by defeating Novak Djokovic in a hard-fought five-set match. Despite dealing with health issues and requiring medical aid, Djokovic showcased his legendary tenacity, coming back from two sets down. However, Navone executed his tactics flawlessly and remained focused, marking a career-defining victory against one of the sport's greatest players.

title: Stranger ran past Nepal school screaming ‘run, water’. It saved 370 kids, teachers
content: An unidentified man's warning saved over 370 pupils and teachers from a massive flood. Students and staff scrambled to a forested hill as floodwaters surged rapidly. Communications were disrupted, making it difficult to account for all students after the event. One father tragically perished while attempting to reach the school for his son. The school continues efforts to trace pupils and reunite them with their families.

title: ‘Everyone is worried’: Pakistan languish at WTC bottom after another heavy defeat
content: Pakistan's Test team faces deep concerns after another heavy away defeat.  Pacer Mohammad Abbas admitted that everyone is worried about the team's current performances.  Dropped catches at Lord's allowed England to score significantly more runs.  The team's batting, bowling, and fielding are all areas needing improvement.  Pakistan's young pace attack is still adjusting to Test cricket demands.

title: Italy population to shrink by nearly 4 million by 2050 as ageing accelerates
content: Italy's population is projected to significantly decrease by 2050.  Birth rates remain low, while the elderly population is expected to grow.  This demographic shift will create new economic and welfare system challenges.  Southern regions anticipate the most substantial population losses across the country.  Immigration has previously helped stabilize the population figures.

title: Social activist Anna Hazare admitted to hospital in Mumbai
content:
NEW DELHI: Veteran social activist Anna Hazare has been admitted to a hospital in Mumbai, according to reports. Hazare, 89, has been admitted for medical treatment. Hazare, who has been associated with several anti-corruption and social reform campaigns, rose to national prominence during the 2011 anti-corruption movement, when he led a hunger strike demanding a strong Lokpal law.
